Consult Summary:
- Acute diarrheal illness with vomiting and periumbilical abdominal pain for ~3 days; suspected infectious gastroenteritis with risk of dehydration.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Profuse watery/very loose diarrhea and persistent vomiting for 3 days; vomiting started after breakfast this morning (~2 hours prior to consult).
- Symptom details:
  - Diarrhea: began watery, now very loose; frequency today at least four times (patient lost count overall).
  - Vomiting: unable to keep liquids or food down.
  - Fever: patient reports feeling very hot/“boiling” but no thermometer reading.
  - Abdominal pain: central/periumbilical, tender to touch, intermittent crampy pain with urgency to open bowels.
  - Urine: passing urine; last passed approximately 1 hour before consult; patient could not describe urine color.
  - No blood in stool or urine reported.
  - No rash.
- Exposure: Household contact — brother has similar symptoms; brother reports many at his school affected.
- Past medical history:
  - No prior chronic abdominal problems; normal bowel habit (daily once in morning).
  - Occasional menstrual cramps; last period 2 weeks ago.
  - No surgeries reported.
- Medications:
  - Vitamin D, dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Occasional ibuprofen for menstrual cramps, dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Oral rehydration solution (ORS) salt-sugar mix: taken ~three times daily for the past two days.
- Allergies: not documented.
- Social history / preventive care:
  - Non-smoker.
  - Drinks alcohol occasionally ("a pint from time to time").
  - Lives with brother and mother.
  - Occupation: graphic designer; working from home today due to illness.
  - Not on contraception; not sexually active.

Examination:
- (No formal examination or vital signs documented.)

Impression:
- Probable infectious gastroenteritis (doctor suspects viral etiology but bacterial infection not excluded).
- Ongoing vomiting and diarrhea with potential risk of dehydration.

Plan:
- Arrange urgent clinic appointment for:
  - Clinical assessment of hydration status.
  - Collection and prompt submission of a stool sample for testing to exclude bacterial infection.
- Patient advice given:
  - Continue ORS in very small, frequent sips to maintain hydration (patient advised to persevere despite vomiting).
  - Eat bland, simple foods if tolerated (toast or biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, milk while symptomatic.
  - If symptoms worsen or patient becomes more unwell, attend A&E urgently.
- Administrative:
  - Appointment to be booked via support line (doctor/clinic to arrange an urgent appointment).
  - Patient instructed to call back or attend A&E if deteriorates.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies not documented.
  - Full current medication list and dosages not documented (vitamin D and ibuprofen listed without dose/route/frequency).
  - Vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate) not recorded.
  - No formal physical examination findings documented by clinician.
  - No pregnancy test or pregnancy status documented (patient of reproductive age, not on contraception).
  - No laboratory or stool test results available.
  - No explicit discharge safety-netting details (timing for reassessment) beyond general A&E advice.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Minor wording conflict: patient initially said “past couple of days” and later specified “three days ago” for symptom onset (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall intelligible with a few short pauses and minor inaudible segments; sufficient clinical detail captured.
